items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: I had Joe Avery and, and we were coming up there.

ctx.x: Oh, well, when they started, first I heard it was in New York in 45. I went up at Bunk Johnson. I used to go over there by this fellow there, what you call him, the guitar player, what his name is? The one who has a nightclub up there? Yeah, right around the corner from us. What his name was? Eddie? Eddie Connors, yeah. He's a little bit around the corner from him. And that's where I heard the Wild Bill Davidson, because there was scooching every fellow, you understand? Solo. But the whole time we was up there,…

You know, when I used to go up to Tyler's Big Auden in 1945, you weren't even here then, but you were in New York, I guess. I had Joe Avery and, and we were coming up there. I never heard a solo the whole time I was there. Not one solo. The trumpet would take down and that was all.

Well, and now, now I see, you're just switching to the truth. Now you take, now you take, but Lewis, Lewis Armstrong would tell you himself. The time that, when he was, when he was playing, when he was playing here. When he was at the Dixieland bands, there's no trumpet tape, no solo bar himself, or a clarinet, or a trombone. Sometimes the music would call for, sometimes three or four bars solo, something like that. Three or four bars. Some others would take it, you see. But now like, you play a solo, I take one,…
